_status: DRAFT. Closes the code-side blocker on OI-005. Every item carries reviewStatus 'needs_review' and MUST be reviewed under DEP-003 before baseline. The scoring thresholds in particular are a reasoned starting point, not a validated instrument.
_source: Adapted from the sebum-production axis of the Baumann Skin Type framework (REF-004, CC BY). The full Baumann instrument resolves 16 types across four axes; this uses only the dry/oily axis, because SRS 4.2 defines exactly four SkinType values and the other three axes have no consumer in this system.
_designNotes: Questions ask about OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR over time, never about appearance in a photograph. FR-ONB-006's rationale is that skin type reflects sebum production across days, while an image captures one moment confounded by lighting and recent cleansing.

Scoring lives here rather than in Python so that CON-003 holds: no clinical judgement is encoded in application code. Changing a weight is a content change, reviewable by a practitioner who does not read Python.
The T-zone axis is separate from the oil axis on purpose. COMBINATION is not 'a bit oily' -- it is oily in one region and not another, and a single summed score cannot express that.

scoring._comment: Evaluated in order. First matching rule wins. The order is the tie-break policy and is deliberate: COMBINATION is tested first because a combination profile also produces a moderate oil score and would otherwise be absorbed into OILY.

rules.rationale: Oil concentrated in the T-zone with dryness elsewhere. Both signals must be present; T-zone shine alone is not combination skin.
Oil signal clearly dominates. The margin of 3 rather than 1 keeps a near-tie out of a definite classification.

Fallback. Neither signal dominates and no regional split. NORMAL is the residual category, not a positive finding -- an unconditional final rule is what guarantees the scorer is total, so no answer set can leave a user without a type.

questions.prompt: A few hours after washing your face, how does it usually feel?
By the middle of the day, where does your skin look shiny?
How often do you notice flaking or rough patches on your cheeks?
Where can you see your pores most clearly?
